programme_facts.value: The module is designed to serve as an introduction to basic concepts and theories in linguistics. The various subfields and branches of linguistics will be introduced and discussed in class lectures.

metadata.chunk_title: Module Code - Title: + Year Last Offered: + Hours Per Week: + Grading Type: + Prerequisite Modules: + Rationale and Purpose of the Module:

programme_facts.value: The module comprises four distinct but interrelated themes, each dealt with in sequential blocks over the twelve week module.

metadata.chunk_title: Syllabus: + Learning Outcomes:

programme_facts.value: Nature of language and linguistics: Introduction to basic concepts in linguistics, including language, duality, arbitrariness.

metadata.chunk_title: Syllabus: + Learning Outcomes:

programme_facts.value: Phonetics & Phonology: Recognition and categorization of the sounds of English and other languages.

metadata.chunk_title: Syllabus: + Learning Outcomes:

programme_facts.value: Morpho-Syntax: Focus on how words are formed and how they combine to make sentences.

metadata.chunk_title: Syllabus: + Learning Outcomes:

programme_facts.value: Semantics and Pragmatics: Focus on meaning and its relevance to the study of language.

metadata.chunk_title: Syllabus: + Learning Outcomes:

programme_facts.value: 2 of the languages listed, available at advanced level; French, German, Japanese, and Spanish also available at beginners' level.

metadata.chunk_title: Pathways and Electives for Applied Languages + What you will study + Semesters 1, 2 and 3:

programme_facts.value: An additional language from the initial list, Law, Marketing, or Politics and International Relations.

metadata.chunk_title: Pathways and Electives for Applied Languages + What you will study + Semesters 1, 2 and 3:

programme_facts.value: Literature in one of the languages you are studying or Introduction to New Media and Cultural Studies.

metadata.chunk_title: Pathways and Electives for Applied Languages + What you will study + Semesters 1, 2 and 3:

programme_facts.value: Building a foundation in two (or three) chosen languages and the societies in which these languages are spoken, as well as in Linguistics and elective subjects.

metadata.chunk_title: Pathways and Electives for Applied Languages + What you will study + Semesters 1, 2 and 3:

programme_facts.value: First three semesters spent in UL.

metadata.chunk_title: Pathways and Electives for Applied Languages + What you will study + Semesters 1, 2 and 3:

programme_facts.value: You will spend semesters 4 and 5 away from UL. You will be on a work placement for the first semester (cooperative education) and you will be studying in a university for the second semester (external academic placement).

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: Working and studying abroad gives you a fantastic opportunity to deepen your linguistic skills and cultural knowledge.

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: Students generally divide their time between their two main languages.

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: If German and Spanish are your main languages, you could spend your cooperative education in Spain or Argentina for example and spend your external academic placement in a German-speaking country.

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: If you are studying Irish, you may be working in the Gaeltacht or in Irish-medium schools and media organisations.

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: You will get plenty of advice and guidance about these choices and you will start planning them well in advance.

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 4 and 5:

programme_facts.value: a deeper understanding of the historical, political, economic and cultural factors that have shaped the societies in which your two languages are spoken

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: continuing the study of these languages to a high level of proficiency

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: specialised, advanced skills such as interpreting and translating

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: continue the study of your third language/politics and international relations/marketing, or specialise in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages or Technical Communication

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: study literature modules in your second language

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: choose from a variety of interesting electives in the areas of linguistics, media, sociology, literature and film

metadata.chunk_title: Semesters 6, 7 and 8:

programme_facts.value: Understand the purpose of linguistic study, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics.
